title: Functions and Modularity: Reusable, Readable Code

questions.question: The DRY principle states that:
options: Code should run without water cooling
Every piece of knowledge should live in exactly one place
Functions should always be tested twice
questions.rationale: Don't Repeat Yourself means one definition, many callers — so a bug is fixed once and every caller benefits.

questions.question: What is the difference between parameters and arguments?
options: Parameters are the names in the definition; arguments are the values passed in the call
Parameters are values; arguments are names
Arguments exist only for keyword calls
questions.rationale: The recipe lists ingredients (parameters); the kitchen receives the food (arguments) — definition-side names versus call-side values.

questions.question: Inside a function, *args collects extra positional arguments into a:
questions.rationale: *args gathers surplus positional arguments into a tuple; **kwargs gathers surplus keyword arguments into a dict.

questions.question: Inside a function, **kwargs collects extra keyword arguments into a:
questions.rationale: Double-star parameters catch name=value pairs, so kwargs behaves like a dictionary of keyword extras.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the LEGB scope rule?
questions.rationale: Python searches Local first, then the Enclosing function, then the Global (module) scope, then Built-ins — the first match wins.

questions.question: A function that ends without executing a return statement returns:
questions.rationale: A function with no return (or a bare return) yields None — the classic cause of 'the variable is None' bugs.

questions.question: What does a docstring do?
options: Comments the function out of the program
Is stored in __doc__ and shown by help() and IDEs
questions.rationale: A string on the first line of a function becomes its __doc__ attribute, surfaced by help() and documentation tools.

questions.question: The main danger of `from module import *` is that it:
options: Runs the import twice as slowly
Disables type hints in the file
Can silently overwrite your own names with the module's
questions.rationale: Star imports dump every public name into your namespace, so a collision overwrites your name without any error until something misbehaves.

questions.question: A Python package is:
options: A directory of modules containing an __init__.py, imported with dots
A zip archive installed with pip
A module with more than ten functions
questions.rationale: A package is a folder of modules with __init__.py that enables dotted imports such as myapp.io.readers; a single .py file is a module.

questions.question: The global keyword is needed inside a function to:
questions.rationale: Reading a global needs no declaration, but assignment creates a local unless you declare global x to rebind the module-level name.
